pr.title: Depend on GitHub's gh-stack skill instead of vendoring it
pr.head: 1cc47342dba3d5eed61f3efc44dcc89405eb3ed0

summary: Projector's implement, fix-pr, and start-fix-loop skills open and maintain stacks: chains of pull requests, each based on the branch below it, that GitHub records as one unit. They drive stacks with gh stack, a GitHub CLI extension, and GitHub publishes a gh-stack skill that teaches an agent its commands.

Until now Projector shipped its own edited copy of that skill under skills/gh-stack/. Every upstream release meant diffing the copy and reapplying the edits by hand, and upstream's v0.2.1 rewrite left the copy a release behind. This pull request deletes the copy and depends on upstream instead.

1. Packaging. The Projector marketplace serves upstream's skill, unmodified and pinned to tag v0.2.1 and its commit, as a second plugin named gh-stack. The projector plugin declares it as a dependency, so a fresh Claude Code install of projector installs gh-stack too.
  2. Projector's rules. The edits the copy carried become rules in implement's "Stack dependent work" section that win over upstream's skill: split only at the reviewability ceiling, open every layer as a draft, replace the body gh stack submit writes, and never merge.
  3. Documentation. docs/plugins.md and the website say where the skill now comes from, and how Codex, which has no plugin dependencies, can add it by hand.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One open finding: install.sh upgrades an installed plugin with claude plugin update, which does not install the new dependency, so an existing user loses the skill on upgrade. See the flag on .claude-plugin/plugin.json.
  • The first head carried four commits that merged separately as #217; this head is rebased onto main and holds only the unvendoring commit.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Vendored: a copy of another project's files kept in this repository.
  • Marketplace: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json catalog Claude Code installs Projector's plugins from.
  • git-subdir source: a marketplace entry that installs one directory of another Git repository at a given ref.
  • Layer: one pull request in a stack.

groups.title: Install upstream's skill as a dependency
groups.kicker: The marketplace serves upstream's skill and the projector plugin depends on it
intro: Claude Code installs plugins from a marketplace. Projector's marketplace used to list one plugin, projector, whose skills/ tree included the copied gh-stack skill. It now lists a second plugin, gh-stack, whose source is the skills/gh-stack directory of github/gh-stack at tag v0.2.1, with the commit pinned as well. The projector plugin names it in dependencies.
A newer upstream reaches users only when a Projector change moves that ref and sha. Codex has no plugin dependencies, so its manifest is unchanged and the packaging test checks that it declares none.

checks.text: In an empty Claude Code config, claude plugin install projector@projector from this head also installs gh-stack@projector, and claude plugin details gh-stack@projector lists one skill, gh-stack. Tag v0.2.1 of github/gh-stack resolves to the pinned commit.

files.note: Adds the gh-stack plugin entry, sourced from upstream's repository at a pinned tag and commit.

checks.text: The ref and the sha must name the same commit. The packaging test checks only their shapes, so a release that moves one must move the other.

files.note: Declares gh-stack as a dependency of the projector plugin.

checks.text: Open finding: an existing install never receives this dependency. install.sh moves an installed plugin forward with claude plugin update projector@projector, which does not install a newly declared dependency, so an upgrade removes the copied skill and installs nothing in its place. Running claude plugin install projector@projector after the update does install it.

files.note: The copied skill, deleted. Its Projector-specific edits reappear as rules in implement.
Drops gh-stack from the published skill set and checks the new dependency, the pinned source, and that Codex declares no dependencies.

groups.title: Keep Projector's stack rules in implement
groups.kicker: The edits the copy carried become rules that win over upstream's skill
intro: The copied skill differed from upstream in four ways that matter to Projector's review loop. Since upstream's skill now ships unmodified, implement's "Stack dependent work" section states those differences as rules that win wherever the two disagree.

• Split only at the reviewability ceiling. Upstream suggests a new layer when a diff grows large or moves to tests; Projector splits only when one review would hold unrelated arguments, and keeps tests and documentation with their code.
  • Draft every layer. --open readies new and existing layers alike, and only a clean review should mark a layer ready.
  • Replace the generated body. gh stack submit writes a body with a stack footer and no ## Testing section.
  • Never merge. Upstream documents gh stack merge; merging stays the user's checkpoint.

files.note: Points at upstream's skill instead of the deleted file, adds the four rules, and cites upstream's "Exit 3 recovery" for rebase conflicts.

checks.text: Upstream's v0.2.1 SKILL.md has the "Exit 3 recovery" list this line cites, describing gh stack rebase --continue and --abort.
For a branch with more than one commit, submit --auto also titles the pull request with the branch name. This rule covers only the body; the review suggests extending it to the title.

groups.title: Say where the skill comes from
groups.kicker: Plugin documentation and the website describe the dependency
intro: docs/plugins.md explains that Claude Code installs upstream's skill with projector, that the marketplace pins its version, and how a Codex user can add the skill by hand. The website's agents section stops listing gh-stack among the skills the plugin carries.

checks.text: This holds for a fresh install. An existing install upgraded through install.sh does not get the dependency; see the flag on .claude-plugin/plugin.json.

files.note: Says Claude Code installs GitHub's gh-stack skill, instead of listing it as one of the plugin's own skills.
